Modified assessment using the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):

- Policy tone: Hawkish and vigilant. The FOMC acknowledges softening activity but emphasizes elevated inflation, ongoing rate hikes, and continued balance sheet reduction.
- SLOOS context (July 2022): Banks broadly tightened standards and terms for C&I and CRE loans; tightened for residential mortgages (GSE-eligible, jumbo, subprime), HELOCs, credit cards, and subprime auto. Banks increased loan pricing and collateral requirements and cited a weaker economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and liquidity concerns. Demand was mixed: stronger for C&I (including small firms) and HELOCs, but weaker across CRE categories.
- Synthesis: Tighter bank credit supply and higher loan costs amplify the restrictive stance from rate hikes and QT, pointing to softer capex, housing, and CRE activity. Mixed loan demand does not offset the drag from tighter standards. Inflation risks remain to the upside, but the credit channel should increasingly weigh on growth.

Net tone: more negative macro outlook with strong anti-inflation resolve; modestly more negative after incorporating SLOOS tightening.

sentiment score = -0.50
